title: Diffusion
competency: Apply the particle nature of matter to explain diffusion and its everyday effects.

keywords.def: The mixing and spreading out of a substance because its particles move. Particles go from high to low concentration.
How crowded the particles of a substance are in a place.

en.text: Diffusion is the mixing and spreading out of a substance because its particles move. Particles go from where they are crowded to where they are few. Diffusion is very fast in gases, slower in liquids and very, very slow in solids.

screens.title: A smell in the class
screens.ask: Someone opens perfume in one corner of the class. Who smells it first?
screens.after: Students near the bottle smell it first. The perfume particles spread out slowly to the rest of the room.

screens.title: Experiment 2.1: simple experiment on diffusion
paras: Open a bottle of perfume in one corner of the room.
Record how long it takes students at different distances to smell it.
Add 2 or 3 drops of ink to a beaker of water. Watch the colour spread.

screens.caption: A drop of ink slowly colours all the water in a beaker.

screens.title: 2.1.4 Diffusion
paras: The mixing and spreading out of a substance because its particles move is called diffusion.
It is the net movement of particles from high concentration to low concentration.

screens.title: Fast or slow?
table: Very fast: particles move quickly in all directions
Smell of hot sizzling food reaches us far away
A drop of ink colours a beaker of water
Very, very slow: particles hardly move

screens.title: Diffusion in daily life
paras: Tea: a tea bag in hot water colours the water.
Perfume spreads from one part of a room to the rest.
A drop of food colouring colours a glass of water.
An open soda bottle goes flat: carbon dioxide spreads into the air.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The mixing and spreading out of a substance because its particles move. Particles go from high to low concentration.
How crowded the particles of a substance are in a place.

screens.why: Particles spread from where they are crowded to where they are few.
screens.clue: Where are the perfume particles crowded at first?

screens.title: Put in increasing order of the rate of diffusion
screens.why: Diffusion: solids (very, very slow) < liquids (slower) < gases (very fast).
screens.clue: Which state has the fastest particles?

screens.text: A tea bag in hot water colouring the water is an example of diffusion.
screens.why: The tea particles spread through the water.
screens.clue: Do the tea particles spread out?

screens.text: An open bottle of soda goes flat. Why?
opts: Carbon dioxide diffuses out into the air
screens.ans: Carbon dioxide diffuses out into the air
screens.why: The drink has more carbon dioxide than the air. So the gas spreads out into the air.
screens.clue: Where is the gas more crowded: in the drink or in the air?

screens.text: Almaz puts one drop of ink in cold water and one in hot water. Which colours the water first, and why?
opts: Both the same: ink does not move
Neither: ink cannot diffuse in water
screens.why: Heat makes particles move faster, so diffusion is quicker in hot water.
screens.clue: Which postulate is about heat and speed?

screens.title: The particle model
steps: All matter is made of tiny particles.
The particles move all the time.

screens.text: What happens to particles when matter is heated?
screens.clue: Think of hot and cold water.

items.ask: You smell deodorant in the classroom after someone sprays it in the hallway. The ___ moves from high concentration to low concentration.
items.clue: Word box: diffusion, low, scent, high.

items.text: The scent moves from ___ concentration in the hallway to ___ concentration in the classroom.
items.why: It was sprayed in the hallway, so it is crowded there.
Spreading out because particles move is diffusion.

items.title: Arrange in increasing order of the rate of diffusion

test.ask: The spreading out of a substance because its particles move is called ___.

test.text: In which state is diffusion fastest?
test.why: Gas particles move very quickly in all directions.

test.text: Diffusion in solids is very, very slow.
Which is NOT an example of diffusion?
test.why: Freezing is a change of state, not spreading out.

test.text: Why does the smell of cooking wat reach the next room faster than ink spreads in a cup of water?
opts: Gas particles move faster than liquid particles
test.ans: Gas particles move faster than liquid particles
test.why: The smell travels as a gas; diffusion in gases is faster than in liquids.
